title: B2B Industrial: +198% Organic Traffic in Month Two
excerpt: How structural SEO more than tripled sessions for a B2B industrial supplier and held through four Google core updates. Read the case.
rm_desc: B2B industrial SEO more than tripled sessions and held through four Google core updates. Read the case.
content: This b2b industrial SEO case covers a supplier with a technically weak site and almost no organic footprint: 50 organic visitors and 87 sessions in the first month of measurement. The category had demand; the site simply could not be found in it.
How the b2b industrial SEO programme was built

The engagement began with full technical remediation and a rebuild of the site structure, with keyword research run against category and specification-led intent. On-page work followed across heading hierarchy, meta information and keyword density, backed by sustained authority building tracked monthly against a fixed metric set.

Industrial B2B categories tend to have thin, technical search demand with relatively few competing domains, which makes referring backlinks disproportionately powerful once the technical and content foundation is sound. B2B industrial SEO in a category like this rewards patient authority building, industry directories, supplier associations, genuine technical citations, more than the aggressive, high-volume content play that tends to work reasonably well in consumer categories with much broader search demand behind them.
Reporting covered eight metrics every month, with Google algorithm changes annotated directly against them so movement could be attributed honestly.

Month two produced the sharpest movement: organic traffic rose 198% (50 to 149), sessions rose 355% (87 to 396), and referring backlinks grew from 112 to 209. Backlinks reached 10,068 by month eight. Indexed keywords went from zero to ranking, with the first target keyword landing in month four.

The more useful result is what happened next. Four consecutive Google core updates landed during the engagement, August, September, October and November 2023, and the site held. During the August core update it improved in four of six tracked areas; through the September Helpful Content update, which cut visibility across the category, sessions and backlinks continued to climb even as traffic dipped.

Traffic peaked in month five and settled lower through the algorithm turbulence that followed; we reported that decline in the same chart as the growth. Gains this steep also reflect a low base and a site whose underlying content deserved to rank once the structure stopped hiding it, the same work on a thin site would have moved very little. What this b2b industrial SEO engagement demonstrates is durability through algorithm change, which is harder to achieve than a single good quarter.
Why it held through four core updates

Google's documented core update guidance consistently points toward the same underlying signals: genuine expertise, real usefulness to the searcher, and technical soundness. B2B industrial SEO built on those fundamentals rather than a specific ranking trick tends to hold through updates aimed at removing exactly the shortcuts this engagement never took. Sites that spiked quickly on thinner, more fragile tactics tend to be exactly the ones that fall hardest whenever the next update eventually lands.
